mainTopic: The sources for קידושי כסף and קידושי ביאה, and why the תורה writes a פסוק when a קל וחומר seems to prove the same law
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer: the extra words 'ויצאה חנם' teach that even an איילונית can be sold as a maidservant and goes free at בגרות. The גמרא then explains that we only say 'the תורה just wrote out a קל וחומר' when no new lesson can be found in the words. Next, a ברייתא learns קידושי כסף from the word 'כי יקח' in the פסוק about divorce, linked to 'קח' when אברהם bought the field from עפרון. The ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed when a קל וחומר from an אמה העבריה seems to prove the same thing. רב אשי answers that the קל וחומר is weak from its very start, because money can free a maidservant but can never end a marriage. The גמרא then shows why the תורה needed both 'ויצאה חנם' and 'כי יקח'. Finally, the ברייתא learns from 'ובעלה' that ביאה makes קידושין. רב אשי again explains why the פסוק is needed: the קל וחומר from יבמה fails, since a יבמה is already bound to the יבם and an ordinary woman is not.

steps.title: The extra words 'ויצאה חנם' teach a new law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the extra words 'ויצאה חנם' are needed to teach something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'And she shall go out for nothing' come to teach us this new point.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous lines. It says the extra words 'ויצאה חנם' are not wasted, because they teach a new law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, מר בר רב אשי argued that a קל וחומר already proves that reaching adulthood (בגרות) frees a maidservant. That made the פסוק seem extra. The answer is that the פסוק teaches something the קל וחומר could not: even an איילונית, who never shows the normal signs of growing up, can be sold, and she goes free when she reaches adulthood.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes to teach us (a new point)
'And she shall go out for nothing', the פסוק about a Hebrew maidservant going free
A woman who never develops the normal signs of maturity

phrases.english: It teaches us
'Then she shall go out for nothing,' etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous section about why the extra words are needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra פסוק a new job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'ויצאה חנם' seemed extra, because a קל וחומר already proves that בגרות frees her.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words teach that an איילונית can be sold and goes free at בגרות.

steps.title: Doesn't the תורה sometimes write out what a קל וחומר already proves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges מר בר רב אשי: we have a rule that a פסוק may write out something a קל וחומר could prove, so why look for a new job for the extra words?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to מר בר רב אשי, who said 'Isn't it a קל וחומר?', there is a problem. We have a rule that the פסוק sometimes takes the trouble to write out something that could be learned from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on מר בר רב אשי. Why did he need to find a new lesson in the extra words?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בר רב אשי treated the extra words as if they could not just repeat what the קל וחומר teaches. But there is a known rule that the תורה sometimes writes a law out even when a קל וחומר could prove it. So it seems he could have left the words as simply repeating the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument, reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one
The פסוק took the trouble to write it out

phrases.english: And according to Mar bar Rav Ashi, who said:
'But isn't it a kal vachomer?'
But we say
that a matter that can be learned through a kal vachomer,
the verse still takes the trouble and writes it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the method behind the answer in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's assumption that the extra words must have a new lesson
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה sometimes writes out what a קל וחומר proves, so the words could simply be repeating it.

steps.title: That rule is only used when there is no other answer
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a פסוק may repeat a קל וחומר is only a last resort. If we can find a new lesson in the words, we do.
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only where there is no other way to explain the פסוק. But where there is another way to explain it, we use that explanation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Saying 'the פסוק just repeats the קל וחומר' is a last resort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We only say the תורה wrote out a קל וחומר when we cannot find any other lesson in the words. Here we can: the איילונית law. So מר בר רב אשי was right to give the words a new job.

keyTerms.meaning: This rule applies only...
To give a different answer or explanation
We answer that way

steps.whatToRemember: The idea that 'the תורה wrote out a קל וחומר' is a last resort. If a פסוק can teach something new, we read it that way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading פסוקים all over the ש״ס: we try to find a new lesson in every word before calling it a repeat.

phrases.english: That applies only where there is no other way to answer,
but where there is another way to answer,
we answer that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any extra פסוק could just be repeating a קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: We only say that when no other lesson can be found in the פסוק.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns קידושי כסף from 'כי יקח'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a תנא who has a different source for betrothal with money: the word 'יקח' (takes) in the פסוק about divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא learns it from here, as a ברייתא teaches: 'When a man takes a woman and lives with her, and if she does not find favor in his eyes because he found in her...' The word 'taking' always means with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now opens a new section. It brings a ברייתא with a different source for the law that a woman can be betrothed with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא learned קידושי כסף from other sources. Now a תנא points to the word 'כי יקח' in the פסוק about divorce and says that 'taking' means taking with money.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא brings it from here (a different source)
'Taking', from the word 'יקח'
Betrothal done by giving money

phrases.english: And a tanna brings it from here,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the law that a woman can be betrothed with money.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:
'When a man takes a woman and lives with her,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה אִם לֹא תִמְצָא חֵן בְּעֵינָיו
phrases.english: and it will be, if she does not find favor in his eyes,
because he found in her, etc.'
'Taking' means only with money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, different source for קידושי כסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'יקח' in the פסוק teaches that a woman can be betrothed with money.

steps.title: Proof that 'taking' means money, from אברהם's field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that 'קיחה' means money from אברהם's words to עפרון: 'I will give money for the field, take it from me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And so the פסוק says: 'I have given money for the field; take it from me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up its claim that 'taking' means money. It points to a פסוק where 'take' is clearly linked to paying money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When אברהם bought the field from עפרון, the word 'קח' was used together with paying money. So the same word 'יקח' in the פסוק about marriage is understood as taking with money too.

keyTerms.meaning: And so the פסוק says (bringing support)
The field אברהם bought from עפרון

steps.whyThisMatters: This link between 'קח' here and 'קח' at the field of עפרון is the famous source for קידושי כסף.

phrases.english: And so it says:
'I have given money for the field; take it from me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 4 that 'קיחה' means money.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק about אברהם buying the field from עפרון

steps.title: Why do we need a פסוק? A קל וחומר from an אמה העבריה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: why do we need a פסוק at all, when a קל וחומר from a Hebrew maidservant proves that a woman can be acquired with money?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it logical? A Hebrew maidservant cannot be acquired through relations, yet she can be acquired with money. This woman can be acquired through relations, so isn't it logical that she can be acquired with money too?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own source. It says logic alone, a קל וחומר, should teach that a wife can be acquired with money, so the פסוק seems unneeded. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמה העבריה cannot be acquired through relations, so she is the 'weaker' case for being acquired, and still money works for her. A wife can be acquired through relations (ביאה), so she is the 'stronger' case. If money works in the weaker case, it should surely work in the stronger one.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it logical? (opening a קל וחומר)
A Hebrew maidservant
Relations, one of the ways to betroth a woman
Is acquired

steps.confusionAlert: The question here is not whether money works for קידושין. Everyone agrees it does. The question is only why we need a פסוק when logic seems to prove it.

phrases.english: But isn't it logical?
Just as a Hebrew maidservant,
who cannot be acquired through relations,
can be acquired with money,
this one, who can be acquired through relations,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is a woman being betrothed as a wife.

phrases.english: isn't it logical that she can be acquired with money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the source given in steps 4 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'כי יקח' as the source for קידושי כסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from an אמה העבריה (no ביאה, yet money works) to a wife (ביאה works) proves that money works, so a פסוק is unnecessary.

steps.title: A יבמה seems to break the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא attacks the קל וחומר. A יבמה becomes married to the יבם through ביאה, yet she cannot be acquired with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: A יבמה proves otherwise: she is acquired through ביאה, but she is not acquired through money!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tries to knock down the קל וחומר from אמה העבריה. It points to a יבמה, who can be acquired through ביאה but not through money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that any woman who can be acquired in a strong way can also be acquired with money. A יבמה breaks that pattern, because ביאה works for her but כסף does not. So a woman is not necessarily acquired with money just because other methods work.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died without children, who is bound to marry his brother (the יָבָם)
Will prove (otherwise). This is the standard way of bringing a counter-example to a קל וחומר.
Intimacy, one of the ways a marriage is made

phrases.english: A yevama proves otherwise,
for she is acquired through intercourse
and yet she is not acquired through money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר from אמה העבריה that was raised in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר that a woman can be acquired with money
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A יבמה is acquired through ביאה but not through money, so the pattern the קל וחומר relies on does not hold.

steps.title: The יבמה is different because a שטר does not work for her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the יבמה counter-example. A יבמה cannot be acquired with a שטר, but an ordinary woman can, so she is closer to the money-acquisition pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a יבמה? She cannot be acquired with a document. Can you say the same about this woman, who can be acquired with a document?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back against the יבמה attack. It shows that a יבמה is a special case and cannot disprove the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה is weaker in how she can be acquired, since a שטר does not work for her. A regular woman can be acquired through a שטר, so she is a stronger case than the יבמה. Because of this, the fact that money does not work for a יבמה says nothing about a regular woman, and the קל וחומר stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: What about X, since X is special in this way? This formula points out what makes a case different.
A document, one of the ways a marriage is made
Will you say the same about this one?

phrases.english: What about a yevama?
She is special, since she cannot be acquired through a document.
Will you say the same about this woman,
who can be acquired through a document?

steps.triggerLanguage: מה ליבמה שכן אין נקנית בשטר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counter-example from step 7, which restores the קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A יבמה lacks שטר, so she is a weaker case than a regular woman and cannot disprove the קל וחומר.

steps.title: The ברייתא still brings the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by bringing the פסוק 'כי יקח איש' as the source for קידושי כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'When a man takes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by quoting the פסוק as its source. This sets up the גמרא's next question, because the קל וחומר seemed to survive the attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר was defended in step 8. Even so, the ברייתא still relies on 'כי יקח איש'. That looks unnecessary, and the גמרא will now ask about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says. This introduces the verse that serves as the source.

phrases.english: The verse states: "When a man takes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא's discussion by citing the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא's source for קידושי כסף is the פסוק 'כי יקח איש'.

steps.title: Why is the פסוק needed if the קל וחומר works?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed when the קל וחומר already proves קידושי כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק for this? It already comes from the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The קל וחומר survived the attack, so why bring a פסוק at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the attack from יבמה was pushed away, so the קל וחומר should be enough on its own. A פסוק for the same law looks extra, and the גמרא wants to know what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a פסוק?
It comes, meaning it is already learned (from the קל וחומר)

phrases.english: Why do I need a verse for this?
It is already derived!
phrases.notes: He means it is already learned from the קל וחומר, which stood up to the יבמה attack.

steps.triggerLanguage: הא למה לי קרא הא אתיא לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא in step 9 cites a פסוק after the קל וחומר was defended.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'כי יקח איש'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר survived the יבמה attack, so the פסוק seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב אשי: the קל וחומר was flawed from the start
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the קל וחומר has a weakness built into its very foundation, so the פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: because one can say that there is a refutation at the very root of the argument.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question. The קל וחומר can be broken from the very beginning, so we cannot rely on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבמה attack failed, but that does not save the קל וחומר. רב אשי says the comparison itself, between a regular woman and an אמה העבריה, is weak from the outset. He explains how in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a reason that knocks down a קל וחומר
From the root of the argument, from its very starting point

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Because one can say
that there is a refutation at the very root of the argument.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אשי משום דאיכא למימר מעיקרא דדינא פירכא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Undermines the קל וחומר at its foundation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the יבמה attack failed, the קל וחומר works and no פסוק is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר is weak from the start, so the פסוק is needed.

steps.title: A maidservant can go free with money, but a wife cannot
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains the weakness. An אמה העבריה can buy her freedom with money, so it makes sense that money also acquires her. A wife cannot be released with money, so the פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do you learn it from? From an אמה העבריה. But what about an אמה העבריה? She can go out with money. Can you say the same about this woman, who cannot go out with money? Therefore the פסוק says: 'When a man takes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי spells out the flaw in the קל וחומר. Once it falls, we need the פסוק 'כי יקח איש' after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money is tied to an אמה העבריה at both ends: money brings her in, and money can set her free. A wife is never released with money; she leaves only with a גט or when her husband dies. Because of this difference, we cannot learn a wife from an אמה העבריה, and the פסוק has a real job.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish maidservant, a young girl sold by her father
Goes free with money. For a wife, this would mean being released from the marriage.
From where are you bringing it?

steps.whatToRemember: The קל וחומר from אמה העבריה fails because money can free her but can never end a marriage. So קידושי כסף must come from the פסוק 'כי יקח איש'.

phrases.english: From where are you deriving it?
From a Hebrew maidservant.
But what about a Hebrew maidservant?
She is special, since she can go free with money.
Will you say the same about this woman,
who cannot go free with money?
Therefore the verse states: "When a man takes."

steps.triggerLanguage: מהיכא קא מייתית לה מאמה העבריה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the foundational flaw that רב אשי mentioned in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a key difference between the two cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A woman can be learned from an אמה העבריה.
steps.terutzMaskana: An אמה העבריה is different because money can free her. So the פסוק 'כי יקח איש' is needed.

steps.title: Why the תורה needed both פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both 'ויצאה חנם' and 'כי יקח איש' are needed. If the Torah had written only 'כי יקח', we would think the קידושין money always belongs to the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write 'ויצאה חנם', and it was necessary to write 'כי יקח איש'. If the Torah had written only 'כי יקח', I would have said that the קידושין money the husband gives her is hers. So the Torah wrote 'ויצאה חנם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the Torah needed both פסוקים. It starts with what we would wrongly think if we had only 'כי יקח'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כי יקח איש' teaches that money makes קידושין. It does not tell us who keeps that money. Without 'ויצאה חנם' we would say the money always goes to the woman, so that פסוק is needed to teach that the father has a right to it when she is young.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
She shall go out for free (a פסוק about the אמה העבריה)
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two questions. 'כי יקח איש' answers whether money makes קידושין. 'ויצאה חנם' is needed for a different question: who gets the money.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "Then she shall go out for free,"
and it was necessary to write "When a man takes."
For if the Merciful One had written only "When he takes,"
I would have said:
the betrothal money that the husband gives her
is hers,
so the Merciful One wrote "Then she shall go out for free."
phrases.notes: This teaches that while she is still young, her father gets the money, not her.

steps.triggerLanguage: ואיצטריך למיכתב ויצאה חנם ואיצטריך למיכתב כי יקח איש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting 'כי יקח איש' as the source for קידושי כסף, the גמרא explains why the Torah also needed 'ויצאה חנם'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both פסוקים are needed. 'ויצאה חנם' prevents the mistake that קידושין money always belongs to the woman.

steps.title: Why 'ויצאה חנם' alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written only 'ויצאה חנם', we might think a woman could give money to a man and marry him. So the Torah wrote 'כי יקח', meaning 'he takes', not 'she takes'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah had written only 'then she shall go out for nothing,' I would have said that where she gave him money and betrothed him, it counts as קידושין. So the Torah wrote 'when he takes' and not 'when she takes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the point from the last step about why both פסוקים are needed. This half explains what 'כי יקח' adds that 'ויצאה חנם' alone could not teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ויצאה חנם' alone does not say who gives the money to whom. So we might think a woman can marry a man by giving him money. The words 'כי יקח' (he takes) teach that the man must be the one doing the קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
She shall go out for nothing (שמות 21:11)
When he takes (the man is the one who acts)
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

steps.whatToRemember: Both פסוקים are needed. 'כי יקח' teaches that the man gives and the woman receives. The other פסוק fills in what 'כי יקח' alone would leave out, which was explained in the previous step.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "then she shall go out for nothing,"
I would have said:
where she gave it to him, she to him,
and betrothed him, it would be a valid betrothal.
So the Merciful One wrote "when he takes"
and not "when she takes."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״וְיָצְאָה חִנָּם״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided explanation begun in step 13 of why both פסוקים are needed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a man can make קידושין. A woman who gives a man money does not marry him.

steps.title: The source that a woman can be married through ביאה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word 'ובעלה' that a woman can be married through ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And has relations with her' teaches that a woman can be acquired in marriage through ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to the second way of making קידושין, which is ביאה. It brings the word 'ובעלה' as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is still working through the פסוק in דברים 24:1. 'כי יקח' was the source for כסף. Now 'ובעלה' becomes the source for ביאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And has relations with her (דברים 24:1)
Marital relations, one of the three ways to make קידושין
Teaches

phrases.english: "And has relations with her"
teaches that she is acquired through relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: after finishing כסף, the ברייתא turns to ביאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman can be married through ביאה, learned from 'ובעלה'.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from יבמה seems to make the פסוק unneeded
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether logic alone proves ביאה. A יבמה cannot be acquired with money but is acquired through ביאה. So a regular woman, who can be acquired with money, should surely be acquired through ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a logical argument? A יבמה cannot be acquired with money, yet she is acquired through ביאה. So this woman, who can be acquired with money, should surely also be acquired through ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own source. It asks why we need 'ובעלה' if a קל וחומר already proves ביאה works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument says a יבמה is the 'weaker' case, because money does not acquire her, and yet ביאה does. A regular woman is the 'stronger' case, because money does acquire her. So ביאה should certainly work for her too.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it logical? (opens a קל וחומר)
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
A widow whose husband died without children, who marries his brother

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical argument?
If a יבמה, who is not acquired with money,
is acquired through relations,
then this woman, who is acquired with money,
isn't it logical that she is acquired through relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the פסוק in step 15 is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from יבמה would already prove that ביאה makes קידושין, so the פסוק seems extra.

steps.title: אמה העבריה seems to break the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: An אמה העבריה is acquired with money but not through ביאה. So being acquired with money does not prove that ביאה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Hebrew maidservant proves otherwise: she is acquired with money, and yet she is not acquired through ביאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests the קל וחומר and offers a case that seems to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that if money works, ביאה should work too. An אמה העבריה shows that money can work while ביאה does not. So that assumption looks false.

keyTerms.meaning: A Hebrew maidservant
Will prove (a case that breaks an argument)

phrases.english: A Hebrew maidservant will prove otherwise,
since she is acquired with money
and is not acquired through relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 16 using a case that breaks it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being acquired with money does not always mean ביאה works too.

steps.title: אמה העבריה is different because she is not acquired for marriage
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the אמה העבריה case. She is acquired as a servant, not as a wife, so it makes sense that ביאה does not acquire her. A wife is acquired for marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about an אמה העבריה is that she is not acquired for marriage. Can you say the same about this woman, who is acquired for marriage?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא defends the קל וחומר by pushing back on the אמה העבריה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביאה is a marriage act. So it fits that ביאה does not acquire someone who is bought as a servant. A woman being married is acquired for אישות, so the אמה העבריה case does not apply to her, and the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (a way to point out a difference)
For the purpose of marriage
Her acquisition

phrases.english: What is special about a Hebrew maidservant
is that she is not acquired for marriage.
Will you say the same about this woman,
who is acquired for marriage?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְאָמָה הָעִבְרִיָּה, שֶׁאֵין קִנְיָנָהּ לְשׁוּם אִישׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attack in step 17, so the קל וחומר of step 16 still holds.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The אמה העבריה case used to break the קל וחומר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An אמה העבריה is not acquired for marriage, so she does not compare to a wife.

steps.title: The ברייתא still brings the פסוק 'ובעלה'
steps.stepSummary: Even though the קל וחומר seems to survive, the ברייתא ends by bringing the פסוק 'ובעלה' as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And has relations with her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes this section by bringing the פסוק anyway. This sets up the גמרא's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as step 9 with קידושי כסף. The קל וחומר seemed to work, yet the ברייתא still relies on a פסוק. That makes us ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the verse says

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "And has relations with her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא's section on ביאה, mirroring step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source for קידושי ביאה is the פסוק 'ובעלה'.

steps.title: Why is a פסוק needed if the קל וחומר works?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs 'ובעלה' when the קל וחומר already proved ביאה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק? It already comes from the קל וחומר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ending. This is the same question it asked about כסף in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rejected the אמה העבריה attack, so the קל וחומר seemed to stand. If logic alone proves ביאה, the פסוק looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a verse?
It already comes (from the logic)

phrases.english: But why do I need a verse?
It already comes from the logic!
phrases.notes: He means the קל וחומר from יבמה that survived the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמָה לִי קְרָא, הָא אָתְיָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ending of step 19, just as step 10 questioned step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר survived the challenge, so a פסוק should not be needed.

steps.title: רב אשי: the קל וחומר is weak because it starts from יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the קל וחומר is weak at its very root. Its starting point is יבמה, and he begins to show the problem there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Because one can say there is a weakness at the very root of the argument. Where are you learning it from? From יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins his answer by pointing to the base of the קל וחומר, the case of יבמה. The full explanation of why יבמה is a weak base comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches רב אשי's answer for כסף in steps 11-12. There he found a weakness in the case the argument was built on. Here too he is not attacking the logic of the comparison, but the יבמה case it starts from.

keyTerms.meaning: A weakness at the very root of the argument
Where are you learning it from?

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Because one can say
there is a weakness at the root of the argument:
Where are you learning it from?
From יבמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר מֵעִיקָּרָא דְּדִינָא פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20, using the same method as steps 11-12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a weakness in the base case of the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר from יבמה proves ביאה, so the פסוק is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר is built on יבמה, which is a weak base. So the פסוק is needed. The details are explained next.

steps.title: A יבמה is already bound, so she cannot be the source
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out what makes a יבמה special: she is already tied to the יבם and waiting for him. An ordinary woman is tied to no one, so ביאה working for a יבמה does not prove it works for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about a יבמה is that she is already bound to the יבם and waiting. Can you say the same about this ordinary woman, who is not bound and not waiting for anyone?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows why the starting point of the קל וחומר, which is יבמה, does not carry over to an ordinary woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said: if ביאה acquires a יבמה, it should surely acquire a regular wife. רב אשי answers that a יבמה is already connected to the יבם through the Torah, so ביאה only finishes a bond that already exists. An ordinary woman has no bond at all, so ביאה might not be strong enough to create one from nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died with no children, who must marry his brother or receive חליצה
Bound or tied to someone
And she stands, meaning she is already waiting in that state
What is special about this case, since... (a way of pointing out a difference)
Would you say? (asking if the same rule really applies to the new case)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say the earlier steps were wrong to reject the other challenges. רב אשי is attacking the very first case the קל וחומר was built on, so the whole proof falls, no matter how well it held up against the other questions.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the ברייתא brought the פסוק at all. A קל וחומר is only as strong as its starting case.

phrases.english: What is special about a יבמה?
That she is already bound and waiting.
phrases.notes: He means she is already tied to the יבם before he does anything, just by the Torah's rule.

phrases.english: Would you say the same about this one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is an ordinary woman who is not a יבמה.

phrases.english: who is not bound and not waiting?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's answer from step 21 by naming the exact weakness in the יבמה case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire קל וחומר, by knocking out its starting case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A יבמה is already bound to the יבם, so ביאה only completes an existing bond; an ordinary woman has no such bond.

steps.title: So the source is the פסוק 'ובעלה'
steps.stepSummary: Since the קל וחומר cannot stand, the ברייתא needs the פסוק 'ובעלה' to teach that ביאה acquires a wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says: 'and he has relations with her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question from step 20: the פסוק is needed because logic alone could not prove that ביאה works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 the גמרא asked why the ברייתא brought 'ובעלה' if the קל וחומר already worked. Now we see the קל וחומר breaks down at its root, so the only real source is the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the Torah source)
And he has relations with her; the source that ביאה acquires a wife

steps.whatToRemember: ביאה acquires a wife because of the פסוק 'ובעלה', not because of a קל וחומר. The קל וחומר from יבמה fails since a יבמה is already bound to the יבם and an ordinary woman is not.

phrases.english: Therefore the פסוק says: 'And he has relations with her.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of רב אשי's answer: with the קל וחומר gone, the פסוק is necessary.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The source that ביאה acquires a wife is the פסוק 'ובעלה', because the קל וחומר from יבמה is not reliable.
